name: Husarln
description: Husarln is a three-player Austrian tarock game linked to the Illustrated Tarock branch. It is played with a 42-card reduced tarock pack and puts heavy pressure on trump distribution and tactical contract play.
deck: 42-card Industrie und Glueck tarock deck variant

history.origins: Husarln appears in tarot-family references as a regional tarock game in the broader Industrie und Glueck tradition.
timeline: Historical period: regional tarock variants develop in central Europe.
Modern references: Husarln is listed in tarot family indexes and reference collections.
history.cultural: Husarln belongs to the coffeehouse and club tarock culture where accurate counting and disciplined trump play decide long sessions.
history.evolution: The game shares core Austrian tarock mechanics while preserving local table conventions for contract flow and counting.

setup.players: Three players compete in rotating declarer versus defenders flow.
setup.deck: 54-card Industrie und Glück pack with 22 permanent trumps and 32 suited cards.
setup.dealing: Cards are dealt with a talon packet according to local rules before contract decisions and trick play.

rules.objective: Win enough card points under the chosen contract by taking tricks and controlling key trumps.
rules.gameplay: Players follow suit when possible, otherwise play trump when required, and otherwise discard. Highest trump wins trumped tricks; otherwise highest card in the led suit wins. Contract and talon handling determine risk and reward each deal.
keyRules: Three-player tarock with contracts and tarot trump hierarchy.
Suit-follow obligations apply before discretionary discard.
Talon decisions influence declarer strength and defender counterplay.

strategy.basic: Preserve high trumps and avoid conceding point-rich tricks early.
strategy.intermediate: Use talon information to rebalance suit length and create controlled trump entries.
strategy.advanced: Optimize contract selection against hand texture and expected defender pressure while counting trumps and honors.
tips: Do not overcommit trumps before point-critical tricks.
Track exposed honors to estimate remaining trick equity.
